item.title: DIY Telescope Mount GOTO Systems: OnStep vs OpenAstroTracker vs EQMOD for Self-Hosted Astronomy Control
item.description: A telescope mount that automatically finds and tracks celestial objects transforms amateur astronomy. Instead of star-hopping with finder charts, you select a target on your phone or laptop and the mount slews to it, then tracks it precisely as Earth rotates. Three open-source platforms let you build or upgrade your own GOTO system: OnStep (Arduino-based telescope controller), OpenAstroTracker (3D-printed star tracker), and EQMOD (ASCOM driver for commercial equatorial mounts).

item.title: Self-Hosted Astrophotography Automation: INDI Server vs KStars/Ekos vs PHD2
item.description:
What Is Astrophotography Automation?

Astrophotography automation turns a complex multi-step imaging workflow into a coordinated, repeatable process. Instead of manually adjusting your telescope mount, focusing, and triggering exposures throughout a cold night, you run a self-hosted server — typically on a Raspberry Pi mounted at the telescope — that orchestrates camera control, mount tracking, autoguiding, and image capture.
